module_title: Name Reactions, Chemical Tests & Aldol/Cannizzaro Mechanics (Intermediate)
introduction: This intermediate tier focuses on the most highly-tested organic reactions in competitive exams. It covers the precise mechanics of Aldol and Cannizzaro reactions, and the crucial laboratory tests used to visually distinguish between different types of carbonyl compounds.

core_concepts.title: Aldol Condensation
core_concepts.description:
Requires: Carbonyl compound with at least ONE $\alpha$-hydrogen. Reagent: Dilute Base (e.g., $dil. NaOH, Ba(OH)_2$).
Mechanism: The base removes the acidic $\alpha$-hydrogen, forming a resonance-stabilized enolate ion. This enolate acts as a nucleophile and attacks the carbonyl carbon of a second, un-ionized molecule. The initial product is a $\beta$-hydroxy aldehyde (Aldol). Upon heating ($\Delta$), it undergoes dehydration (loses water) to form an $\alpha,\beta$-unsaturated carbonyl compound.

core_concepts.title: Cannizzaro Reaction
core_concepts.description:
Requires: Carbonyl compound with ZERO $\alpha$-hydrogens (e.g., $HCHO$, $Ph-CHO$). Reagent: Concentrated Base (e.g., 50% $NaOH$ or $KOH$).
Mechanism: It is a Disproportionation reaction (simultaneous self-oxidation and self-reduction). One molecule is oxidized to a carboxylic acid salt ($R-COO^-Na^+$), while the second molecule is reduced to a primary alcohol ($R-CH_2OH$).

core_concepts.title: Tollens' Test (Silver Mirror Test)
core_concepts.description:
Reagent: Ammoniacal Silver Nitrate $[Ag(NH_3)_2]^+$ in alkaline medium. 
Purpose: Distinguishes Aldehydes from Ketones. 
Reaction: Aldehydes (both aliphatic and aromatic) are easily oxidized to carboxylate ions. The $Ag^+$ is reduced to metallic Silver ($Ag$), which deposits on the test tube walls as a brilliant silver mirror. Ketones DO NOT respond to this test.

core_concepts.title: Fehling's Test
core_concepts.description:
Reagent: Fehling A (aq. Copper sulfate) + Fehling B (Rochelle salt / sodium potassium tartrate in strong base). 
Purpose: Aldehydes reduce the blue $Cu^{2+}$ complex to a red-brown precipitate of Cuprous Oxide ($Cu_2O$). 
Exception: AROMATIC aldehydes (like Benzaldehyde) DO NOT respond to Fehling's test. It only works for aliphatic aldehydes.

core_concepts.title: Iodoform Test (Haloform Reaction)
core_concepts.description:
Reagent: Iodine and Sodium Hydroxide ($I_2 + NaOH$, or $NaOI$).
Purpose: Identifies the presence of a **Methyl Ketone** group ($CH_3-C=O$) or a secondary alcohol that oxidizes to it ($CH_3-CH(OH)-$).
Reaction: The methyl group is fully halogenated and then cleaved off, precipitating as **Iodoform ($CHI_3$)**, a distinct bright YELLOW solid with an antiseptic smell.

important_entities.name: Cross-Aldol Condensation
important_entities.key_fact: Reaction between two completely different aldehydes/ketones.
important_entities.significance: If both molecules contain $\alpha$-hydrogens, a messy mixture of FOUR different products is formed (2 self-aldol, 2 cross-aldol). However, if one molecule lacks an $\alpha$-hydrogen (like Benzaldehyde) and the other has one (like Acetophenone), it yields a single, highly conjugated major product (e.g., Benzalacetophenone), which is synthetically very useful.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: Students often memorize that the Iodoform test is exclusively for 'Ketones'. This is false. The test is for the $CH_3-C=O$ structural unit. Therefore, **Acetaldehyde ($CH_3-CHO$)** gives a positive Iodoform test. In fact, it is the ONLY aldehyde that gives a positive Iodoform test. All other aldehydes fail.

mnemonics_and_tricks.memory_phrase: Line up the Alpha H2 with the Carbonyl O
mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: To directly predict the final Aldol Condensation product without drawing the intermediate: Take Molecule 1 and expose its $C=O$ oxygen. Take Molecule 2 and expose its two $\alpha$-Hydrogens ($H_2$). Erase the $H_2$ and the $O$ to make $H_2O$, and connect the remaining fragments with a double bond ($C=C$).

exam_strategy_tips: When a question asks you to distinguish between Pentan-2-one and Pentan-3-one, immediately use the Iodoform test. Pentan-2-one is a methyl ketone and will give a yellow precipitate. Pentan-3-one is an ethyl ketone and will not.
